sources.reading_verification: Inspected the complete relevant sections in the full local extracted text. §1.1.1 identifies z=x+iy with (x,y) and gives coordinate arithmetic. §2.1.2 writes real differentiability with the |h| remainder quotient; §2.2.2 treats Wirtinger operators through the real coordinates. The library item proves the general coordinate transport directly and does not import the source's holomorphicity hypotheses.

sources.title: L. V. Ahlfors, Complex Analysis, 3rd ed.
sources.locator: Chapter 4, §1.2, printed pp. 104-105 (PDF pp. 119-120), rectifiable arcs and coordinate bounded variation.
sources.reading_verification: Inspected the full-text PDF extraction of §1.2. It defines complex arc length as the supremum of polygonal chord sums, defines rectifiability by finiteness, compares those sums with coordinate variation sums, and states the real/imaginary bounded-variation criterion. The current item supplies a complete typed proof using the library's proved R^2 criterion rather than relying on the source's abbreviated comparison.

contents.name: Complex rectifiability and coordinate bounded variation
contents.support: The source states the coordinate BV criterion; the local theorem proves exact partition-sum equality and invokes the fully proved library R^2 criterion.

alternatives.argument: For each partition, the coordinate isometry identifies every complex chord modulus with the Euclidean chord norm, so the same partition sums and their suprema agree. Apply the inspected published theorem thm-rectifiable-iff-coordinate-functions-have-bounded-variation to the coordinate path for both directions. For the speed formula, apply cor-piecewise-c1-paths-have-additive-speed-integral-length on the same finite subdivision and write the Euclidean norm as sqrt(x_prime^2+y_prime^2). Ahlfors §1.2 independently states the complex coordinate-BV criterion. This is a complete local proof and does not rely on Shastri.
